title: omx-contract vocabulary
description: GENERATED by `omx-contract render --target json` from data/: one enum per codes and words item of the vocabulary (docs/data-layout.md), for a schema that references the words instead of repeating them. GPL-3.0-or-later.

CURVE_AXES.description: The axes a curve kind is drawn on, each with its unit and how a host draws it (docs/curves.md). A curve's values are in these units, so the drawn values can be held equal to the closed form a kernel's controls give.

text.en: Frequency, on the points of EQ_CURVE_GRID where the curve is a response.
The magnitude of a response at a frequency: 0 dB is unity, a boost positive, a cut negative.
The level a gain computer reads, the static law's input.
The level the static law gives for an input level; the diagonal is no gain change.
A memoryless shaper's input sample, linear, -1 to +1 full scale: bipolar, so an even/odd asymmetry shows.
The shaper's output sample for an input amplitude, linear, on the same full scale.
The time after the dry sound at which a delay's tap or repeat sounds.
The time after an impulse over which a reverb's energy decays.
A level relative to the dry input: 0 dB is the input's own, a tap or a decay below it negative.
The position within one period of a modulation source, 0 to 1.
A modulation source's output at a phase, -1 to +1, before the depth scales it.
The pitch played into a pitch effect, semitones from an origin the host picks.
The pitch the effect sounds for an input pitch, semitones on the same origin: an unshifted map is the diagonal.

CURVE_KINDS.description: The kinds of picture a plugin's panel section draws and a console's card shows, each with the two axes it is drawn on (docs/curves.md). A kernel file and a plugin declaration name a kind by its word; a host keeps only its kind-to-drawing map. Append-only: a kind is never renamed, moved or removed while a reader draws it.

text.en: An EQ's summed magnitude response over log frequency.
A gate's or a compressor's static law, input level to output level, with the live needle.
A memoryless shaper's transfer, input sample to output sample over full scale.
A delay's taps and repeats, each a line at its time and level.
A reverb's decay envelope after an impulse.
The wet path's comb or notch response at the current sweep position (chorus, flanger, phaser, doubler).
A modulation source over one period (tremolo, rotary).
A pitch effect's map from the input pitch to the output pitch.

MACHINE_CLASS_FIELDS.description: What identifies the machine a figure was taken on (plugin-qualify#115): a verdict for a host profile reads only figures of the class it names.

text.en: The machine architecture, as uname -m names it.
The CPU family and model.
The core count, as a band of MACHINE_CORE_BANDS.
The clock, as a band of MACHINE_CLOCK_BANDS.
Whether the kernel is PREEMPT_RT.
Whether the deep idle states are limited.

MACHINE_PROFILE_FIELDS.description: How the machine was set when a figure was taken: the frequency policy and isolation a figure depends on.

text.en: The CPU frequency governor in effect when the figure was taken.
Whether turbo or boost clocking was enabled when the figure was taken.
Whether simultaneous multithreading was enabled when the figure was taken.
Whether the measuring thread ran under real-time preemption, or scheduled as any other thread.
The CPU idle driver or policy in effect when the figure was taken.

MACHINE_CORE_BANDS.description: The bands a machine's core count falls in, ascending.

text.en: A machine with 1 to 2 cores.
A machine with 3 to 4 cores.
A machine with 5 to 8 cores.
A machine with 9 to 16 cores.
A machine with 17 to 32 cores.
A machine with 33 or more cores.

MACHINE_CLOCK_BANDS.description: The bands a machine's clock falls in, ascending.

text.en: A machine clocked under 1.5 GHz.
A machine clocked from 1.5 to 2.5 GHz.
A machine clocked from 2.5 to 3.5 GHz.
A machine clocked from 3.5 to 4.5 GHz.
A machine clocked at 4.5 GHz or more.

MACHINE_ARCHES.description: The architectures a host profile names, as uname -m spells them.

text.en: An x86-64 machine, as uname -m spells it.
An AArch64 machine, as uname -m spells it.

MACHINE_CLASSES.description: The machine classes a host profile budgets for (plugin-qualify#114, #115): the desk, and the Raspberry Pi 4 and 5 a small console runs on.

text.en: An x86-64 desk.
A Raspberry Pi 4, aarch64.
A Raspberry Pi 5, aarch64.

MEASUREMENT_DIMENSIONS.description: The measurable dimensions a measurement document declares it covers: latency and cost since the format's 1.0, stability, RT safety and features since 1.1, for the hosting verdict.

text.en: How long a plugin takes to produce its first sound after it is driven or played.
How much CPU time a plugin spends per block under a sustained stimulus.
Whether a plugin instantiates, processes and tears down without crashing or producing non-finite output.
Whether a plugin's audio thread avoids locks, allocation and other calls a real-time thread must not make.
What capabilities a plugin declares and a prober can confirm, beside latency, cost, stability and RT safety.

MEASUREMENT_UNMEASURED_KINDS.description: What an absent figure means for a merge, the one distinction that changes behaviour: a property of the plugin, a failure of this run, or a dimension the run did not cover.

text.en: A property of the plugin: any prober on any machine reaches it, so it may override a figure.
A property of this run: it says nothing about the plugin and never overrides a figure.
The run did not cover this plugin or this dimension: a partial run, not a finding.

MEASUREMENT_UNMEASURED_REASONS.description: Every reason a figure may be absent, each of its kind: an outcome a sweep produced, never a hypothetical. A reader that meets a reason it does not know treats it as probe-failed.

text.en: No audio input port: nothing to drive.
No audio output port: nothing to read.
Driven, and silent under a stimulus that should have passed.
Needs a second audio input the prober did not supply.
A convolver needing an impulse response the prober did not load.
An instrument that is silent under notes until a sample, a sound font or an instrument file is loaded, which the prober did not load.
The files the host loads cannot be pinned.
An instrument whose voice-info declares a capacity of 0.
An instrument whose note input reads no dialect the prober speaks.
An instrument that declares no voice capacity, run with no probe count.
The plugin would not instantiate at this rate or block size.
The probe worker died while hosting the plugin.
The probe passed its per-plugin time limit.
The output held NaN or infinity.
The plugin is not installed on this machine.
An LV2 worker interface with work or work_response NULL.
A failure with no more specific reason; its own words are kept beside it.
The run did not cover this plugin for this dimension.

MEASUREMENT_LATENCY_METHODS.description: How a latency figure was taken. note-onset is an instrument's: a held note's first sound.

text.en: The delay from a unit impulse to the first output sample above the residual floor: what the plugin does.
Read from the plugin's own latency report: what it claims.
The delay from a note on to the first output sample above the floor.

MEASUREMENT_COST_METHODS.description: How a cost figure was taken.

text.en: A percentile of per-block wall time under a sustained stimulus, warm-up discarded, in nanoseconds per sample.

MEASUREMENT_LATENCY_SCALING.description: How latency moves with the sample rate, derived from readings at several rates, never assumed from a plugin's name.

text.en: The same frame count at every rate.
The same milliseconds at every rate.
No latency a mix can notice at any measured rate.
Fits neither law at a magnitude that reaches a mix: flagged, never averaged.
One usable reading: no law can be fitted.
No rate produced a figure.

MEASUREMENT_LATENCY_SCALING_NOTES.description: Why a derived scaling class is not the naive fit over every reading.

text.en: The readings fit no law but every one is inside the latency budget: the detector's noise.
Only a reading below the operational rates breaks the law; it stays as information.

MEASUREMENT_LATENCY_EXCLUSIONS.description: Why one rate's reading was left out of the fit and of every rate resolution.

text.en: Zero frames at this rate while another rate measured non-zero.

MEASUREMENT_VOICE_BASES.description: Where the number of notes an instrument's cost was measured with came from: the voice capacity the plugin declares (CLAP voice-info), or a count the caller gave.

text.en: The voice capacity the plugin declares through CLAP's voice-info extension.
A note count the caller gave the prober, not read from the plugin.

MEASUREMENT_VERDICT_RATINGS.description: The four ratings a verdict speaks, in order from the best.

text.en: The plugin meets the host profile's budget on every measured dimension.
The plugin meets the host profile's budget only under a stated condition.
Not enough was measured to rate the plugin against the host profile.
The plugin does not meet the host profile's budget on at least one measured dimension.

PANEL_FAMILIES.description: The panel families of a plugin (omx-panel docs/panel-layout.md): the kind of processor its panel is laid out for. The words and their order are the contract; omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs FAMILIES and the skin package schema read them, and keep their code.

text.en: A plugin with no family: its panel is laid out from its groups and its roles.
A gate's or an expander's panel family.
A compressor's panel family.
A limiter's panel family.
A de-esser's panel family.
An equaliser's panel family, parametric or graphic.
A filter's panel family.
A saturator's or a distortion's panel family.
A chorus's, a flanger's, a phaser's or a tremolo's panel family.
A delay's panel family.
A reverb's panel family.
A pitch shifter's panel family.

PANEL_STANDARD_WIDGETS.description: The standard widgets a panel picks from a descriptor and a representation (a skin) draws, in the order omx-panel's tools/panel-description.mjs STANDARD_WIDGETS lists them.

text.en: A travel, drawn as a knob.
A travel drawn long, as a fader.
A toggle, drawn as a switch.
An integer travel or labelled values, drawn as a selector.
A readout, drawn as a meter.
A response or transfer curve, drawn as a graph.
Two controls drawn together as one point on a plane.
A value shown as text.

PANEL_WIDGETS.description: The widgets a declared panel may name for a control, and the extension serves (org.openmixer.panel-description/1): auto leaves the choice to the panel layout. The four others are the shared widgets of omx-panel's schema/panel.schema.json.

text.en: Left out of a panel declaration: the layout picks the widget from the control.
A rotary control.
A linear control.
A two-state control.
A control that picks one of a few values.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_AUDIO_EFFECT.description: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature audio-effect: every kind of effect, a filter, a dynamics processor, a modulation or a space, and the channel-less roles of a processor (utility, mixing, mastering).

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature audio-effect: any audio effect with no more specific feature declared.
The CLAP plugin feature chorus: an effect that thickens a sound with detuned, delayed copies of it.
The CLAP plugin feature compressor: an effect that narrows a sound's dynamic range.
The CLAP plugin feature de-esser: an effect that tames sibilance in a voice.
The CLAP plugin feature delay: an effect that repeats a sound after a gap.
The CLAP plugin feature distortion: an effect that adds harmonics by overdriving a sound.
The CLAP plugin feature equalizer: an effect that shapes a sound's frequency balance.
The CLAP plugin feature expander: an effect that widens a sound's dynamic range.
The CLAP plugin feature filter: an effect that removes or shapes a band of frequencies.
The CLAP plugin feature flanger: an effect that sweeps a short, modulated delay against the dry sound.
The CLAP plugin feature frequency-shifter: an effect that shifts every frequency of a sound by the same amount.
The CLAP plugin feature gate: an effect that mutes a sound below a level.
The CLAP plugin feature glitch: an effect that cuts, stutters or corrupts a sound on purpose.
The CLAP plugin feature granular: an effect built from short grains of a sound.
The CLAP plugin feature limiter: an effect that holds a sound under a ceiling.
The CLAP plugin feature mastering: an effect meant for a mix's final stage.
The CLAP plugin feature mixing: an effect meant for use while mixing, such as a channel strip.
The CLAP plugin feature multi-effects: several effects combined in one plugin.
The CLAP plugin feature phase-vocoder: an effect built on a phase vocoder, typically to stretch or shift a sound independently of pitch and time.
The CLAP plugin feature phaser: an effect that sweeps notches through a sound with an all-pass filter chain.
The CLAP plugin feature pitch-correction: an effect that pulls a sound's pitch toward a scale.
The CLAP plugin feature pitch-shifter: an effect that changes a sound's pitch without changing its duration.
The CLAP plugin feature restoration: an effect that removes noise, clicks or other damage from a recording.
The CLAP plugin feature reverb: an effect that adds the reflections of a space to a sound.
The CLAP plugin feature transient-shaper: an effect that reshapes a sound's attack and sustain.
The CLAP plugin feature tremolo: an effect that modulates a sound's level over time.
The CLAP plugin feature utility: a plugin that does audio housekeeping rather than a creative effect.
The LV2 plugin class AllpassPlugin: an all-pass filter, which shifts phase without changing level.
The LV2 plugin class AmplifierPlugin: a plugin that changes a sound's level.
The LV2 plugin class BandpassPlugin: a filter that passes one band of frequencies.
The LV2 plugin class ChorusPlugin: an effect that thickens a sound with detuned, delayed copies of it.
The LV2 plugin class CombPlugin: a comb filter, which adds a short delayed copy of a sound to itself.
The LV2 plugin class CompressorPlugin: an effect that narrows a sound's dynamic range.
The LV2 plugin class ConverterPlugin: a plugin that converts a signal from one representation to another.
The LV2 plugin class DelayPlugin: an effect that repeats a sound after a gap.
The LV2 plugin class DistortionPlugin: an effect that adds harmonics by overdriving a sound.
The LV2 plugin class DynamicsPlugin: an effect that changes a sound's dynamic range.
The LV2 plugin class EQPlugin: an effect that shapes a sound's frequency balance.
The LV2 plugin class EnvelopePlugin: a plugin that follows or applies an envelope over time.
The LV2 plugin class ExpanderPlugin: an effect that widens a sound's dynamic range.
The LV2 plugin class FilterPlugin: an effect that removes or shapes a band of frequencies.
The LV2 plugin class FlangerPlugin: an effect that sweeps a short, modulated delay against the dry sound.
The LV2 plugin class GatePlugin: an effect that mutes a sound below a level.
The LV2 plugin class HighpassPlugin: a filter that passes frequencies above a cutoff.
The LV2 plugin class LimiterPlugin: an effect that holds a sound under a ceiling.
The LV2 plugin class LowpassPlugin: a filter that passes frequencies below a cutoff.
The LV2 plugin class MixerPlugin: a plugin that combines several signals into one.
The LV2 plugin class ModulatorPlugin: a plugin that modulates one signal with another.
The LV2 plugin class MultiEQPlugin: a multi-band equaliser.
The LV2 plugin class ParaEQPlugin: a parametric equaliser.
The LV2 plugin class PhaserPlugin: an effect that sweeps notches through a sound with an all-pass filter chain.
The LV2 plugin class PitchPlugin: a plugin that changes or tracks a sound's pitch.
The LV2 plugin class ReverbPlugin: an effect that adds the reflections of a space to a sound.
The LV2 plugin class SimulatorPlugin: a plugin that models a physical device or space.
The LV2 plugin class SpatialPlugin: a plugin that places or moves a sound in space.
The LV2 plugin class SpectralPlugin: a plugin that processes a sound in the frequency domain.
The LV2 plugin class UtilityPlugin: a plugin that does audio housekeeping rather than a creative effect.
The LV2 plugin class WaveshaperPlugin: a plugin that reshapes a waveform to add harmonics.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_INSTRUMENT.description: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature instrument: notes in, audio out.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature drum: an instrument that plays drum sounds.
The CLAP plugin feature drum-machine: an instrument that sequences and plays drum sounds.
The CLAP plugin feature instrument: a plugin played by notes, with no more specific kind declared.
The CLAP plugin feature sampler: an instrument that plays recorded samples.
The CLAP plugin feature synthesizer: an instrument that generates its own sound rather than playing samples.
The LV2 plugin class InstrumentPlugin: a plugin played by notes.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_NOTE_EFFECT.description: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature note-effect: notes in, notes out.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature note-effect: a plugin that reads notes and writes notes, such as an arpeggiator.
The LV2 plugin class MIDIPlugin: a plugin that processes MIDI, note in to note out.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_ANALYZER.description: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that become the descriptor feature analyzer: audio in, a reading out (a note detector reads pitch from audio).

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature analyzer: a plugin that reads audio and reports a measurement, with no further output.
The CLAP plugin feature note-detector: an analyzer that reads pitch from audio.
The LV2 plugin class AnalyserPlugin: a plugin that reads audio and reports a measurement.

PLUGIN_FEATURE_OTHER.description: The CLAP plugin features and LV2 plugin classes that fit none of the four feature words: a channel layout stated as a feature (mono, stereo, surround, ambisonic), and the LV2 classes of a generator, an oscillator, a constant and a function, which take no notes and so are no instrument. A scan carries them in the extension bag.

text.en: The CLAP plugin feature ambisonic: a plugin declared to work in an ambisonic channel layout.
The CLAP plugin feature mono: a plugin declared to work in a mono channel layout.
The CLAP plugin feature stereo: a plugin declared to work in a stereo channel layout.
The CLAP plugin feature surround: a plugin declared to work in a surround channel layout.
The LV2 plugin class ConstantPlugin: a plugin with no input that outputs a constant.
The LV2 plugin class FunctionPlugin: a plugin with no audio input or output, used only for its side effects or parameters.
The LV2 plugin class GeneratorPlugin: a plugin with no audio input that generates a sound.
The LV2 plugin class OscillatorPlugin: a generator that outputs a periodic waveform.
The LV2 plugin class Plugin: the base LV2 plugin class, with no more specific class declared.

RESOURCE_KINDS.description: Every resource a host plans a plugin for (FreeMixer/plugin-qualify#116): each measured per machine class, judged per host profile, and unknown, never a pass, when it has no figure.

text.en: The cost per sample at a rate and quantum, its percentile and its tail.
The footprint per instance and its growth over a soak.
The memory a plugin asks of its host for its process call.
The frames a plugin delays its output by, per rate and quantum.
How long a plugin keeps sounding once its input goes silent.
The notes an instrument plays at once.
The wall time of instantiate, activate and the first block.
The threads a plugin starts and their scheduling class, or the host thread pool it asks for.
The work a plugin hands to a non-real-time thread of the host.
The block lengths a plugin accepts.
The file descriptors a plugin holds after activate, and their growth.
The bytes a plugin reads at load and while it processes.
Any socket a plugin opens.
The size of a plugin's saved state, its save and restore time, and its round trip.

RESOURCE_UNITS.description: The units a resource figure is given in; an LV2 unit's name where LV2 has one.

text.en: Nanoseconds per sample.
A count of audio frames.
Milliseconds.
Microseconds.
Seconds.
Bytes.
A plain count, with no unit.
A ratio, with no unit.
A yes or a no: one when the plugin does the thing, zero when it does not.

RESOURCE_BASES.description: How a resource figure was known: what the plugin declares, what a run measured, or a count the caller gave the probe.

text.en: What the plugin declares about itself.
What a run measured.
A count the caller gave the probe.

RESOURCE_MEMORY_PHASES.description: When a plugin's memory is read, per instance (plugin-qualify#114): after instantiate, after activate, at rest after processing, with notes held, and for a second instance, so a shared one-time load is told apart from the per-instance cost.

text.en: Memory read right after the plugin instantiates.
Memory read right after the plugin activates.
Memory read at rest, after processing, with no note playing.
Memory read while notes are held.
Memory read for a second instance, so a shared one-time load is told apart from the per-instance cost.

RESOURCE_UNMEASURED_REASONS.description: Why a resource has no figure a host profile can read, beside the measurement's own reasons (MEASUREMENT_UNMEASURED_REASONS).

text.en: The only figure was taken on another machine class: never read as a pass, never scaled.
The run hit the limit probe isolation set for the resource; the limit is recorded beside it.

RESOURCE_BUDGET_SCOPES.description: What a host profile's budget for a resource is counted over (plugin-qualify#114, #115): one plugin instance, or the whole console.

text.en: Counted over one plugin instance.
Counted over the whole console.

RESOURCE_HOST_ISOLATIONS.description: How a host runs its plugins.

text.en: The host runs its plugins in its own process.
The host runs each plugin in its own process.
The host runs its plugins together in one process apart from its own.

RESOURCE_HOST_LATENCY_HANDLING.description: Whether a host aligns on a plugin's reported latency or only passes it on.

text.en: The host delays every other path to align on this plugin's reported latency.
The host passes the plugin's reported latency on, without aligning other paths to it.

RESOURCE_THREAD_SCHEDULING.description: The scheduling class a host gives its plugin's threads, as the probe output records it.

text.en: No particular scheduling class: the thread runs as any other.
The real-time FIFO scheduling class.

RESOURCE_HINTS.description: What a plugin declares about its own footprint, in openmixer's own hints (FreeMixer/plugin-qualify#116): each a claim plugin-qualify measures and checks, carried by the extension below, as the CLAP draft and as LV2 properties. A hint a plugin does not state is unknown, never zero.

text.en: The memory one instance holds at rest, once activated and idle, with no note playing.
The memory each voice adds while it plays, for an instrument.
The one-time load every instance of the plugin shares, counted once however many are instantiated.
The threads the plugin starts itself, apart from any it asks the host pool for.
Whether the plugin reads from disk while it processes.
Whether the plugin opens any socket.
The wall time of activate and the first block the plugin expects.

SCAN_DOCUMENTS.description: The documents a plugin scan writes, named here and owned elsewhere: the contract names them so the writers and readers cite one word, and keeps no shape of its own for them.

text.en: The JSON document omx-clap-scan writes, one entry per file with its plugins, its parameters and its ports.
The field dump omx-clap-scan --fields writes: a version line, then one scope, field and value record per field a plugin states.

SCAN_FIELD_SCOPES.description: The scopes of a field dump record, as written before the first TAB; an indexed scope is followed by `:<index>`. Named here, owned by their writers: omx-clap-core's scan (docs/scan.md there) and plugin-hostd's field dump (docs/formats.md there) keep the code that writes them.

text.en: The plugin as a whole.
A CLAP parameter, indexed in get_info order.
An audio input port, indexed.
An audio output port, indexed.
A note input port, indexed.
A note output port, indexed.
An LV2 port, indexed by its lv2:index.
The panel description of a plugin that serves org.openmixer.panel-description/1: its family and its fingerprint.
A section of the panel description, indexed.
A control of the panel description, indexed.
A role of the panel description, indexed.
A display of the panel description, indexed.
A per-placement come-up value of the panel description, indexed.

VERB_HOSTS.description: The hosts a verb's implementedBy names (docs/contract-dir.md): the programs a controller sends mod-host's protocol to. A verb states what each one owes it; a host the verb leaves out owes it nothing.

text.en: The daemon that places plugins in workers and answers the verbs it adds itself.
omx-clap-core's worker: a CLAP plugin's host, and an LV2 plugin's through its adapter.
mod-host, the LV2 host whose protocol the others speak.
